subject: computing
subtitle: Using FOR and WHILE loops to repeat instructions efficiently.

data.targetWord: Repeating a block of instructions one or more times; also referred to as a loop

examples.en-GB: Iteration allows a program to print 100 lines using just a few lines of code instead of writing each print statement separately.

data.targetWord: A count-controlled loop that repeats a block of code a fixed, predetermined number of times

examples.en-GB: FOR i ← 1 TO 5 repeats the loop body exactly five times with the counter i taking values 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

data.targetWord: A condition-controlled loop that repeats a block of code as long as its condition remains True; the number of repetitions is not fixed in advance

examples.en-GB: WHILE password != "secret" DO — keeps asking for input until the correct password is entered.

data.targetWord: A loop that repeats a specific, known number of times determined before the loop begins; implemented using a FOR loop

examples.en-GB: Printing the five-times table is count-controlled: we know exactly that 10 lines will be printed.

data.targetWord: A loop that repeats until a condition becomes False; the number of repetitions is not known in advance; implemented using a WHILE loop

examples.en-GB: Asking for a valid score until the user enters a number between 0 and 100 is condition-controlled.

data.targetWord: The variable in a FOR loop that tracks the current iteration number and changes value with each repetition

examples.en-GB: In FOR i ← 1 TO 5, i is the loop variable; it holds 1 on the first iteration, 2 on the second, and so on.

data.targetWord: A variable used to count how many times a loop has run or to track a total; often incremented or decremented inside a loop

examples.en-GB: A counter variable starting at 0 and increasing by 1 each loop iteration can track how many attempts the user has made.

data.targetWord: A loop whose condition never becomes False, causing the program to repeat forever and never move past the loop

examples.en-GB: Forgetting to increment the counter inside a WHILE loop creates an infinite loop because the condition never changes.

data.targetWord: A loop placed inside another loop; the inner loop runs completely through all its iterations for every single iteration of the outer loop

examples.en-GB: A nested loop with an outer loop of 3 iterations and an inner loop of 4 iterations produces 3 × 4 = 12 total inner executions.

data.targetWord: The block of code that is repeated on each iteration of a loop; defined by indentation in Python

examples.en-GB: In a FOR loop that prints numbers 1 to 10, the print statement inside the loop is the loop body.

data.targetWord: The Boolean expression checked by a WHILE loop before each iteration; when it becomes False, the loop ends

examples.en-GB: The condition count <= 5 in a WHILE loop is checked before every iteration; when count reaches 6 the loop stops.

data.targetWord: Increasing a variable's value by a fixed amount, typically 1; used inside loops to make the loop variable progress towards the exit condition

examples.en-GB: count ← count + 1 increments the counter by 1 each time the loop body runs.

data.targetWord: Decreasing a variable's value by a fixed amount, typically 1; used in countdown loops and to reduce a variable towards an exit condition

examples.en-GB: lives ← lives - 1 decrements the lives variable each time the player makes a mistake.

data.targetWord: A Python function that generates a sequence of numbers for use with a FOR loop; range(start, stop) produces numbers from start up to but not including stop

examples.en-GB: range(1, 6) generates the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 — the stop value 6 is excluded.

data.targetWord: A number representing a position in a sequence; commonly used as the loop variable when iterating through items in a list

examples.en-GB: In range(0, 5), the values 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 can serve as index positions to access elements of a list.

data.targetWord: The act of executing the same block of code more than once; iteration is the programming mechanism that achieves repetition efficiently

examples.en-GB: Repetition through a FOR loop avoids writing the same statement ten times; it is written once and repeated automatically.

data.targetWord: The condition that must become False for a WHILE loop to stop; ensuring the exit condition will eventually be met prevents an infinite loop

examples.en-GB: In WHILE count <= 10, the exit condition is count > 10; when count reaches 11 the loop ends.

data.targetWord: A special value entered by the user that signals the end of input and causes a WHILE loop to stop

examples.en-GB: Using -1 as a sentinel value means the program keeps accepting scores until the user types -1 to indicate they are finished.

data.targetWord: A variable that collects a running total by having values added to it on each iteration of a loop

examples.en-GB: total ← total + score adds each score to the accumulator variable total during each loop iteration.

data.targetWord: The result of accumulating values across multiple iterations; a variable used to sum up quantities produced inside a loop

examples.en-GB: After a FOR loop that adds 1, 2, 3, and 4 to a total variable starting at 0, the total is 10.

data.targetWord: A Boolean variable used to record whether a particular condition has occurred; often used to control or exit a WHILE loop

examples.en-GB: A flag variable 'found' set to False before a loop, and changed to True when an item is found, can be used as the loop exit condition.

data.targetWord: The total number of times a loop body executes; for nested loops this is the product of the outer and inner loop counts

examples.en-GB: A nested loop with an outer count of 5 and an inner count of 3 has an iteration count of 15 for the inner body.

data.targetWord: A table used to manually track the value of each variable and any output after each step or iteration of a program

examples.en-GB: A trace table for a FOR loop shows the loop variable and any updated values at the end of each iteration.

data.targetWord: The pseudocode keyword that marks the end of a FOR loop's body, after which the loop variable increments and the condition is re-checked

examples.en-GB: FOR i ← 1 TO 5 ... ENDFOR — ENDFOR marks where the loop body ends and the next iteration begins.

data.targetWord: The pseudocode keyword that marks the end of a WHILE loop's body, after which execution returns to the condition check

examples.en-GB: WHILE count <= 5 DO ... ENDWHILE — execution returns to the WHILE condition after each ENDWHILE.

data.targetWord: A loop that checks its condition before executing the body; a WHILE loop is a pre-condition loop and may never run if the condition is False initially

examples.en-GB: A WHILE loop is a pre-condition loop: if the condition is False before the first check, the body never runs at all.

data.targetWord: A classic example used to demonstrate nested loops: the outer loop controls the row and the inner loop controls the column, printing every product

examples.en-GB: A nested FOR loop with i from 1 to 3 and j from 1 to 3 can print a 3×3 multiplication table.

data.targetWord: A classic example used to demonstrate WHILE loops: the program repeatedly asks for a password until the correct one is entered

examples.en-GB: A password checker using a WHILE loop shows condition-controlled iteration because the number of attempts is unknown in advance.

data.sentence: A FOR loop is a ____ loop because the number of repetitions is known before it starts.
A WHILE loop is a ____ loop because it repeats until a condition becomes False.
You should use a FOR loop when you know the number of repetitions ____, and a WHILE loop when you do not.
An infinite loop occurs when the loop's condition ____ becomes False.
The loop variable in a FOR loop takes a new value at the ____ of each iteration.
A nested loop with an outer loop running 3 times and an inner loop running 4 times executes the inner body ____ times in total.
A WHILE loop checks its condition ____ the body executes on each iteration.
If a WHILE loop's condition is False ____ the first check, the body never runs at all.
In Python, range(1, 6) generates the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, ____.
range(5) in Python generates 0, 1, 2, 3, ____ (five numbers starting from 0).
A variable that collects a running total inside a loop is called an ____.
A ____ value is a special input used to signal the end of user data in a WHILE loop.
A common cause of an infinite loop is forgetting to ____ the loop variable inside the loop body.
A password checker that keeps asking until the correct password is entered is best implemented with a ____ loop.
Printing a times table from 1 to 10 is best implemented with a ____ loop because we know the count in advance.
A multiplication table is an example that uses a ____ loop: one loop for rows, one for columns.
To fix an infinite loop, ensure the variable tested in the condition is ____ correctly inside the loop body.
In pseudocode, the keyword that ends a WHILE loop is ____.
In pseudocode, the keyword that ends a FOR loop is ____.
A Boolean variable used to record whether a certain condition has occurred during a loop is called a ____.

data.title: Trace a FOR loop counting from 1 to 5
data.instruction: Put these trace steps in the correct order.
items: Set the loop variable i to 1 (the start value)
Check whether i is less than or equal to 5 — it is, so enter the loop body
Execute the loop body: print i
Check whether i is still less than or equal to 5 — repeat until i reaches 6
When i equals 6, the condition is False and the loop ends

data.title: Steps a WHILE loop follows on each iteration
data.instruction: Put the steps of a WHILE loop's execution in the correct order.
items: Evaluate the condition to see if it is True or False
If the condition is False, exit the loop and continue after ENDWHILE
If the condition is True, execute the loop body
Update the relevant variable(s) inside the loop body
Return to the condition check at the start of the loop

data.title: Steps to fix an infinite loop
data.instruction: Put the debugging steps in the correct order.
items: Identify which variable is tested in the WHILE condition
Trace through the loop body to check whether that variable is ever updated
If the variable is never updated, add a statement inside the loop body to change it
Check that the update moves the variable towards making the condition False
Re-run the program and verify the loop now terminates correctly

data.instruction: Sort each scenario into the most appropriate loop type.

pairs.text: Keep asking for a password until the correct one is entered
Process each of 30 student names in a register
Keep a game running until the player loses all three lives
Keep reading temperatures until the user enters -999 to stop
Keep asking for a valid score between 0 and 100

data.title: Would this cause an infinite loop?
data.instruction: Sort each loop description into 'infinite loop' or 'terminates correctly'.

pairs.text: count = 1; WHILE count <= 5 DO count = count + 1
count = 1; WHILE count > 0 DO count = count + 1
x = 10; WHILE x > 0 DO x = x - 1
x = 0; WHILE x < 10 DO OUTPUT x (no update to x)
n = 100; WHILE n > 1 DO n = n DIV 2
flag = True; WHILE flag == True DO OUTPUT "hello" (flag never changed)
